links.comparator_used: Anonymized original medical reports as input (full record) versus manually generated case summaries
links.outcome: Agreement with Heart Team (Cohen's kappa), reliability (ICC) and bias toward TAVR (FBI) for guideline-concordant treatment decisions
links.effect: Original reports: kappa −0.47–0.22, ICC 0.0–1.0, FBI 0.95–1.51. Summaries plus guideline knowledge: kappa −0.02–0.63, ICC 0.01–1.0, FBI 0.46–1.23. The two changes were reported together, so the summary effect cannot be separated from the guideline effect.
links.tradeoff: Summaries were generated manually, so the approach needs extensively curated input. Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs, and some responses were unreliable and biased.
links.quote: The LLMs’ performance improved substantially when case summaries were used as input and additional guideline knowledge was added to the prompt (kappa: −0.02–0.63, ICC: 0.01–1.0, FBI: 0.46–1.23).

links.comparator_used: Prompt without added guideline knowledge, using original medical reports as input
links.outcome: Agreement with Heart Team (Cohen's kappa), reliability (ICC) and bias toward TAVR (FBI) for guideline-concordant treatment decisions
links.effect: Original reports: kappa −0.47–0.22, ICC 0.0–1.0, FBI 0.95–1.51. Case summaries plus added guideline knowledge: kappa −0.02–0.63, ICC 0.01–1.0, FBI 0.46–1.23. The guideline effect is confounded with the use of summaries.
links.tradeoff: Hallucinations occurred in all LLMs, and some responses were unreliable and biased even with improved inputs. Performance still depended on extensively curated input.
links.quote: The LLMs’ performance improved substantially when case summaries were used as input and additional guideline knowledge was added to the prompt (kappa: −0.02–0.63, ICC: 0.01–1.0, FBI: 0.46–1.23).
